name: qutb-minar-begun-aibak
description: A Delhi commander started a towering red sandstone minaret beside a new mosque to proclaim the arrival of Muslim rule.

name: iltutmish-caliphal-investiture
description: A robe of honour and a formal letter from Baghdad confirmed a Delhi sultan as a legitimate Muslim ruler of Hindustan.

name: alauddin-khalji-seizes-delhi
description: After a raid on a Deccan kingdom, an ambitious governor killed the sultan who trusted him and took Delhi's crown.

name: alauddin-khalji-takes-chittor
description: A Delhi sultan besieged and took the great Rajput hill fortress, an event later wrapped in legend and epic poetry.

name: firoz-shah-founds-firozabad
description: A sultan built a new walled city on the Yamuna beside Delhi, crowned by a palace with a carved stone pillar on its roof.

name: timur-sacks-delhi-1398
description: A Central Asian conqueror routed the sultan's army and plundered the capital, leaving the sultanate shattered for decades.

name: bahlul-lodi-founds-lodi-dynasty
description: An Afghan chieftain took the throne at Delhi, beginning the last ruling line of the old sultanate.

name: sikandar-lodi-founds-agra
description: A Delhi sultan moved his base to a riverside site on the Yamuna and laid out the city that later became a Mughal capital.

name: sher-shah-defeats-humayun-kannauj
description: An Afghan commander beat the Mughal emperor on the Ganges and drove him into exile, taking the Delhi throne himself.

name: humayuns-tomb-begun
description: A widow of the second Mughal emperor oversaw a garden tomb in red sandstone and marble, a forerunner of the Taj Mahal.

name: battle-haldighati-mughals-mewar
description: Akbar's army, led by a Rajput general, met the Mewar ruler Maharana Pratap in a narrow mountain pass in Rajasthan.

name: jahangir-accession-agra
description: Akbar's son succeeded him at Agra and soon hung a chain of justice outside his palace for any subject to ring.

name: jahangir-marries-nur-jahan
description: The emperor wed a widowed Persian noblewoman who would become the most powerful woman at the Mughal court.

name: peacock-throne-unveiled-shah-jahan
description: A jewelled gold throne, said to have cost twice as much as the Taj Mahal, was first used by Shah Jahan at court.

name: shah-jahan-begins-red-fort
description: The emperor laid the foundations of a vast red sandstone palace-fortress in a new walled capital on the Yamuna.

name: shah-jahan-begins-jama-masjid-delhi
description: Thousands of workers began India's largest mosque opposite the new palace, finished in about six years.

name: aurangzeb-seizes-throne-agra
description: A prince defeated his brothers and imprisoned his ailing father in the fort at Agra, then had himself crowned emperor.

name: badshahi-mosque-lahore-completed
description: A giant red sandstone mosque with marble domes opened at Lahore, among the largest in the world for centuries.

name: aurangzeb-dies-deccan
description: After decades of war in southern India the aging emperor died, and his sons fought over an empire starting to fray.

name: shah-alam-ii-returns-delhi
friendly_name: Shah Alam II Returns to Delhi
description: Escorted by Maratha troops, a Mughal emperor long in exile re-entered his old capital as a figurehead.

name: bahadur-shah-zafar-accession
description: A poet-king inherited the Mughal title, with real power limited to the walls of his palace in Delhi.

name: last-mughal-emperor-deposed
description: After joining a great uprising, the elderly emperor was captured, tried and sent into exile, ending the dynasty.
